segments.name: Total net sales
segments.note: Supermicro reports a single operating segment and printed no product split this quarter. Sales are mostly complete AI server and rack systems (including GB200 and GB300 platforms); services and software were $318M of the total, and one customer accounted for 44.0% of net sales (10-Q).

opex.name: Research and development
opex.note: Designing next-generation servers, racks and Data Center Building Block Solutions; up 31% YoY as hiring rose.

opex.name: Sales and marketing
opex.note: Sales teams and marketing; up sharply YoY as Supermicro hired to support much larger data-center deals.

opex.name: General and administrative
opex.note: Back office, legal and facilities; up 83% YoY, including about $20M more in legal and internal-investigation costs (10-Q).

sources.label: Form 10-Q for the quarter ended Sep 30, 2026 (SEC EDGAR)

verdict: Supermicro's sales nearly quadrupled to $19.9B on demand for GB200 and GB300 AI racks, and a richer product mix lifted gross margin to 12.7%, turning that growth into $1.6B of profit — even though stocking inventory and funding receivables used $434M of operating cash.
otherDetail: Other income was a net $34M expense: $54M of interest income, less $83M of interest expense and $5M of other net expense. A separate $1M share of loss from an equity investee, net of taxes, is shown as equityM (amounts rounded from thousands).
footerNote: Supermicro guided Q2 FY27 net sales to $19.5B–$21.5B and full-year FY27 net sales to $72B–$82B. The Nov 3 release called its figures preliminary; the Nov 6 Form 10-Q confirmed the same income-statement numbers.

kpis.label: Gross margin
kpis.note: vs 9.3% a year ago; 17.5% in Q4 FY26

kpis.label: Cash flow from operations
kpis.note: cash used, despite $1,594M of profit; capex was $42M

follow100Note: Supermicro keeps under $8 of every $100 because the hardware itself costs $87.26 — its model is volume, not margin. Each row is rounded to cents, so the waterfall lands a cent short of the $7.99 kept as profit.

takeaways.title: AI racks nearly quadrupled sales
takeaways.text: Net sales hit $19,946M, up from $5,018M a year ago. The 10-Q attributes the jump mainly to Hyper Servers, GPU and Super Rack billings — up $12,535M, or 293% — led by liquid- and air-cooled GB200 and GB300 systems, on higher volumes and a richer mix.

takeaways.title: Margins are better than a year ago, thinner than last quarter
takeaways.text: Gross margin rose to 12.7% from 9.3% a year ago on product and customer mix, though it fell from 17.5% in Q4 FY26. With operating costs at just 2.4% of sales, that margin still produced $2,064M of operating income.

takeaways.title: Profit did not turn into operating cash
takeaways.text: Operating activities used $434M of cash: receivables grew by $3,560M and inventories by $2,477M to support the sales surge, partly offset by $3,054M more in deferred revenue — money customers paid in advance. Capex was only $42M, so the cash drain is working capital, not factories.
